concept.name: HTTP Semantics & Edge Caching (RFC 9111)

relationships.description: Connects HTTP Semantics & Caching to api gateway in the broader engineering catalog.

concept.tagline: Using Cache-Control freshness lifetimes, ETag/304 conditional validation, and Vary keys so browsers and CDNs offload 70–95% of origin traffic safely.
concept.purpose: Build a progressive mental model of HTTP caching—from no-cache vs. no-store and s-maxage vs. max-age to stale-while-revalidate thundering-herd protection and Vary key normalization.

spark.summary: HTTP caching (RFC 9111) uses explicit freshness lifetimes, validation headers (ETag/Last-Modified), and Vary keys so browsers, CDNs, and reverse proxies serve safe, fast responses without stale leaks.
spark.keyTakeaway: Separate immutable static assets (Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable) from dynamic APIs (Cache-Control: no-cache + ETag revalidation), and use Vary carefully so you never fragment cache hit ratios or leak user-specific responses.
spark.byteSummary:
**Core Mechanics:** Every uncached origin request pays full TLS, application compute, and cross-region RTT (50–250 ms).

**Visual & Structural Flow:** Depicts Browser Cache -> CDN Edge (s-maxage + SWR) -> Origin (304 ETag) (Browser Cache -> CDN Edge POP -> Origin API -> Auth / PII Routes); CDN Stale-While-Revalidate + Collapsed Origin 304 Refresh (Client Browser -> CDN Edge POP -> Origin Server).

**Failure Modes & Application:** Explore cache avalanche/stampede mitigations, multi-tier L1/L2 caching, and HTTP/2 transport.

learningJourney.title: What is RFC 9111 HTTP Caching
learningJourney.explanation:
Every uncached origin request pays full TLS, application compute, and cross-region RTT (50–250 ms). **HTTP caching (RFC 9111)** lets browsers (**private** caches) and CDNs/proxies (**shared** caches) store and reuse responses governed by `Cache-Control`:

- `no-store`: Never write to disk or cache (mandatory for PII/auth).
- `no-cache`: May store, but **must revalidate** with origin (`If-None-Match: "etag"`) before every reuse.
- `public, max-age=31536000, immutable`: Serve for 1 year with zero revalidation (for content-hashed bundles).
- `s-maxage=60, stale-while-revalidate=120`: Shared CDN caches for 60s, then serves stale for 120s while refreshing asynchronously.

sectionDiagram.title: Browser Cache -> CDN Edge (s-maxage + SWR) -> Origin (304 ETag)

cards.label: 304 Bandwidth Savings
cards.detail: ETag validation skips sending the response body when content hasn't changed.

cards.label: Zero PII Leaks
cards.detail: Authenticated endpoints default to Cache-Control: private, no-store.

sectionDiagram.summary: Explicit Cache-Control directives separate 1-year immutable bundles, SWR-cached public APIs, and uncached private endpoints.

learningJourney.title: Why Misconfigured Vary & TTLs Cause Leaks or Stampedes
learningJourney.explanation: Two subtle misconfigurations break production HTTP caches: (1) omitting `private, no-store` on an authenticated route lets a CDN serve User A's profile to User B, and (2) setting `Vary: User-Agent` or `Vary: *` fragments cache keys into thousands of uncacheable variants, collapsing CDN hit ratio to `<5%`.

ideas.title: Normalize `Vary` at the CDN Edge
ideas.description: Normalize `Accept-Encoding` to `{br, gzip, identity}` and strip `Vary: User-Agent` so mobile/desktop browsers share the same cached response.

ideas.title: Thundering Herd Protection with SWR
ideas.description: Pair `s-maxage=60` with `stale-while-revalidate=120, stale-if-error=600` so expired keys refresh in the background without blocking users or hammering origin.

learningJourney.title: Choosing Directives per Endpoint Class
learningJourney.explanation: Every route should belong to one of three explicit caching profiles.

benefits: `public, max-age=31536000, immutable` yields 99%+ cache hit rate and zero conditional 304 round-trips.
costs: Requires build-time content hashing; unhashed `index.html` must use `no-cache`.

benefits: `public, max-age=10, s-maxage=60, stale-while-revalidate=120` absorbs traffic spikes at `<15 ms` p95.
costs: Price or inventory updates take up to `s-maxage` unless actively purged via CDN API.

benefits: `private, no-store` guarantees zero shared CDN caching and zero disk persistence.
costs: Every request hits origin; use internal Redis/app caching behind auth checks if needed.

learningJourney.purpose: Scope boundary: identify where this pattern fits best and where simpler or async alternatives win.

learningJourney.title: Conditional ETag Revalidation & Middleware Defaults
learningJourney.explanation: Enforce `private, no-store` as the safe default in auth middleware, and implement `If-None-Match` strong/weak `ETag` checks on semi-dynamic endpoints to return `304 Not Modified`.
learningJourney.markdownContent:
```http
# 1. Immutable content-hashed bundle
Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable

# 2. Public catalog API with CDN SWR & origin fallback
Cache-Control: public, max-age=10, s-maxage=60, stale-while-revalidate=120, stale-if-error=600
ETag: "v4-9b81c2"
Vary: Accept-Encoding

# 3. Authenticated user profile / checkout state (never cache)
Cache-Control: private, no-store
```

learningJourney.title: Alternatives: Long TTL + Purge vs. no-cache + ETag vs. SWR
learningJourney.explanation: Trade freshness guarantees against origin offload and round-trip latency.

benefits: 95%+ edge offload with near-instant invalidation on CMS/catalog publish.
costs: Purge APIs have rate limits and 1–5s global propagation lag.

benefits: 100% freshness guarantee while saving payload bandwidth via `304 Not Modified`.
costs: Still pays a full network round-trip to origin on every request.

benefits: Zero user-facing revalidation latency; collapses thundering herds on expiry.
costs: First request after TTL sees slightly stale data while background refresh runs.

learningJourney.purpose: The trade-off: compare competing approaches across latency, consistency, and operational cost.

learningJourney.title: Production Edge Flow: SWR Background Revalidation & 304
learningJourney.explanation: With `stale-while-revalidate`, when a cached object's `Age` exceeds `s-maxage` (60s) but is within the `120s` SWR window, the CDN returns the stale response **immediately** (`<15 ms`) and fires a single collapsed async `If-None-Match` request to origin.

sectionDiagram.summary: SWR hides origin revalidation latency from users while collapsed forwarding prevents thundering herds.

knowledgeCheck.question: What is the critical difference between `Cache-Control: no-cache` and `Cache-Control: no-store`?

options.text: `no-cache` allows storing the response but requires origin revalidation (`ETag`/304) before reuse, whereas `no-store` forbids writing the response to any cache
options.feedback: Correct: always use `no-store` (typically `private, no-store`) for sensitive PII or financial responses.

options.text: `no-cache` forbids browser caching, while `no-store` only forbids CDN caching
options.feedback: Both apply to browsers and shared caches; `no-store` is the strict prohibition on storage.

options.text: They are identical aliases in RFC 9111
options.feedback: They have distinct semantics; confusing them is a common source of PII cache leaks.

_recommendedProblem.title: Active-Active Multi-Master Split-Brain Recovery
_recommendedProblem.prompt: Redesign an active-active multi-master relational replication pipeline between us-east-1 and eu-west-1 (6,000 writes/sec, 85 ms WAN RTT, < 15 ms p99 local commit) so a 9-minute transatlantic partition and 180-250 ms NTP clock skew never cause silent Last-Write-Wins (LWW) overwrites.
